To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the environmental impact of the Norwegian economy is increasing, despite a reduction of the environmental impact per unit of production, due to an increase in the consumption of products and services.
the Norwegian economy is on a trajectory towards a sustainable development, as measured by the eco efficiency of production.

The eco-efficiency in production is not sufficient for achieving a sustainable development, and the environmental impact of consumption must be included as an integral part of a sustainability strategy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how the environmental impact of consumption and production has developed in Norway over the last decade, and how this development is related to eco efficiency in production, the ecological footprint of consumption and the development of the wealth of Norwegians.
two questions: (1) How can a more sustainable development be achieved in a rich country like Norway? and (2) What are the implications of the Norwegian case for the global sustainability debate?
the question whether the Norwegian government has been successful in its efforts to achieve sustainable development during the period 1990-2000.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the environmental impact of production has been improved in Norway over the last 10 years, but that the environmental impact from consumption has been increased.
eco-efficiency is a necessary but not sufficient condition for achieving sustainable development.
the Norwegian economy and society are not sustainable in a long-term perspective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
eco-efficiency is a good tool for improving production, but it is not a sufficient tool for achieving a sustainable development.

the eco efficiency strategy, as it has been pursued in Norway, has not been sufficient to ensure a sustainable development, and that the environmental policy should be extended to include consumption.

the environmental policy has been too production oriented and too little focused on consumption, and that the environmental policy should be more focused on the most important environmental problems and the most important environmental actors, i.e. the consumers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the eco-efficiency strategy alone is not enough to ensure a sustainable development.
a sustainable development requires a more holistic approach than the eco efficiency approach.
the environmental impact of consumption is increasing and that the environmental impact is increasing faster than the environmental impact of production.
